title: P0: Hosted API keepalive TTL regression and telemetry ingestion lag postmortem
content:
Summary:

On 2028-07-11 at 02:07 UTC the Hosted API experienced a coordinated latency spike and a short 5xx wave that affected streaming and non-streaming requests for ~27 minutes across us-west1 and eu-west1. Root cause was a recent config change that reduced HTTP keepalive TTL for edge proxies combined with a delayed telemetry ingestion pipeline that hid early signals from the autoscaler and our on-call dashboards. The keepalive/connection churn increased connection establishment latency and increased per-node file descriptor pressure; at the same time telemetry lag prevented proactive autoscaler scale-ups and delayed circuit-breaker alerts.

Impact:
- Duration: ~02:07 UTC -> ~02:34 UTC (27 minutes)
- Regions impacted: us-west1 (major), eu-west1 (minor)
- Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 token latency (stream and non-stream), short 502/504 spikes for streaming sessions, elevated connection reset errors at the edge, many client retries observed
- Customer visible: degraded streaming performance and increased error rates for 18% of active sessions in affected regions. Several large customers opened support tickets.

Detection and response timeline (concise):
- 02:07 UTC: Synthetic streaming checks alert (p99 latency > 2.2s).
- 02:09 UTC: On-call SRE (Devon) sees spike on dashboard; initial hypothesis: autoscaler lag or edge TLS handoff issue.
- 02:11 UTC: Support reports increased customer retries; error traces point to upstream connection resets.
- 02:14 UTC: Investigation shows increased accept/socket churn on edge proxy hosts and elevated ephemeral port allocation.
- 02:18 UTC: Runbook mitigations attempted: increase edge proxy connection pool; no immediate effect.
- 02:23 UTC: Telemetry ingestion backlog discovered (kinesis -> processing cluster) causing 8–12 min lag for metrics feeding into autoscaler. Suspect configuration change deployed 01:55 UTC (edge-proxy keepalive TTL lowered from 120s -> 15s) correlates with onset.
- 02:25 UTC: Emergency rollback of keepalive TTL to 120s rolled out to affected edge pool.
- 02:29 UTC: Telemetry pipeline catch-up initiated (increase consumer parallelism, temporary retention bump).
- 02:34 UTC: Service metrics trend back to baseline; alerts clear.

Root cause analysis (5 whys / contributing factors):
1) Why did we see connection resets and latency? Because edge proxies were closing TCP connections aggressively (keepalive TTL=15s) causing connection churn and more TLS/TCP handshakes per request.
2) Why was TTL set to 15s? A configuration change (edge-proxy tuning PR #2314) intended to free idle connections for a separate bursty workload was rolled out without impact testing on streaming-heavy routes.
3) Why did autoscaler not compensate fast enough? Because the telemetry ingestion pipeline was lagged by 8–12 minutes, so autoscaler decision windows were using stale metrics.
4) Why was the telemetry pipeline lagged? A recent dataflow worker GC/heap regression after a metrics schema change reduced consumer throughput; consumers fell behind at ~01:50 UTC as event volume increased.
5) Why were these two changes allowed to overlap? Lack of coordination between edge proxy tuning and telemetry team rollout; no cross-team preflight that considers streaming workload patterns.

Contributing factors:
- Streaming requests are sensitive to connection churn; lowering keepalive TTL without route-aware testing had outsized impact.
- Telemetry lag masked growing connection error rates in the autoscaler and alerting windows.
- Runbook lacked a short checklist for evaluating keepalive/ephemeral port interactions for streaming routes.
- Monitoring had single-point-of-latency metric (synthetic checks) but internal metric ingestion lag caused delay in scaling and pre-emptive mitigation.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Emergency rollback of edge-proxy keepalive TTL to 120s (02:25 UTC). Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-agent/pull/2314
- Increased telemetry consumer parallelism to force catch-up and temporarily increased retention on the intermediate stream (02:29 UTC).
- Temporarily relaxed circuit-breaker sensitivity for streaming endpoints to avoid aggressive failovers while traffic stabilized (02:20–02:40 UTC).
- Manual warm-up of connection pools on new edge instances (02:27 UTC).

Longer-term corrective actions (action items):
- SRE/Edge: Add a preflight checklist for keepalive/connection TTL changes that includes simulated streaming load and ephemeral port exhaustion modelling. Owner: Priya Nair. Target: 2028-07-25.
- Telemetry: Revert the metrics schema change and patch GC regression in the consumer workers; add more aggressive auto-scaling and self-heal for the telemetry processing cluster. Owner: Luca Romano. Target: 2028-07-18.
- Platform: Implement a telemetry freshness alert (metric ingestion lag > 2m) that is independent of synthetic checks and tied into autoscaler safety policy. Owner: Ava Martinez. Target: 2028-07-15.
- Runbooks: Draft a dedicated runbook section "Connection-churn and keepalive TTL" with step-by-step mitigations and suggested temporary knobs. Owner: Devon Chen. Target: 2028-07-20.
- QA/Release: Require cross-team impact notes on config change PRs that touch edge/telemetry/ingestion. Owner: Release Eng. Target: 2028-07-30.

Post-incident notes and findings:
- Our synthetic checks detected the symptom first, but telemetry lag delayed internal route-level visibility. Lesson: detection plus fast metric freshness must both be prioritized.
- The scale of impact was amplified because streaming sessions keep connections open; a keepalive knob that is fine for short HTTP requests can be catastrophic for long-lived streams.
- Autoscaler reliance on a single metrics pipeline without fallback to active health probes is brittle. Consider lightweight, zero-latency health sampling for autoscaler on critical routes.

Open questions / follow-ups (for engineering discussion):
- Should we expose route-level keepalive policies (per-route TTL) so streaming endpoints can opt-out of aggressive TTLs?
- Is the telemetry pipeline sufficiently decoupled so that a consumer regression can't mask platform health for >5 minutes?
- Do we need an ephemeral port telemetry dashboard to proactively detect OS-level exhaustion patterns?

Appendix (evidence, quick artifacts):
- Graphs: p95/p99 token latency (us-west1) spike plot: confluence link -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/graphs/p0-keepalive-2028-07-11
- Logs: aggregated proxy ECONNRESET sample trace (snippet id): JIRA-INC-4921 -> logs:stream/stream-ecollect/4921
- Deployments: edge-proxy tuning PR merged 01:55 UTC -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-agent/pull/2314
- Telemetry consumer error trace and GC logs: S3:/telemetry/consumers/2028-07-11/gc-dump.log

Runbook draft (short checklist to add to on-call playbook):
1) If synthetic checks show p99 streaming latency > 2s and connection resets appear in proxy logs:
   - Immediately check edge-proxy keepalive TTL config across active pools (kubectl get cm edge-proxy -n infra).
   - Check ephemeral port usage on edge hosts (netstat/ss).
   - Check telemetry ingestion lag (conductor -> metrics-lag metric).
2) If keepalive TTL < 60s on streaming-heavy routes: rollback to previous stable TTL or set route-level TTL to >= 120s.
3) If telemetry lag > 3m, increase telemetry consumer parallelism and page telemetry owner; do not trust autoscaler signals until freshness < 1m.
4) If FD/ephemeral port pressure is high, temporarily increase host ephemeral port range (sysctl) and add connection pool warmup to new instances.
5) Notify support and customers for >10m visible impact and provide ETA.

Ownership and sign-off:
- Incident lead: Ava Martinez (SRE)
- Mitigation lead: Devon Chen (on-call SRE)
- Edge proxy owner: Priya Nair
- Telemetry owner: Luca Romano

Status: in_review. This is a working postmortem; please add comments and link supplementary artifacts.

Notes to self (informal):
- Might be worth a small chaos test to vary keepalive TTLs across a subset of hosts to observe streaming degradation in the staging environment.
- Revisit the autoscaler logic: fallback to synthetic streaming latency probe if metrics freshness is stale.
